chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, from his father, from Fadala, from Aban, who said:

Some of them mentioned at the place of Abu'l-Hasan, peace be upon him, and said: It has reached us that a man perished at the era of Allah's Messenger, Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family, and left behind two dinars, to which Allah's Messenger, Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family, said: «He left a lot». He said: Indeed, that was a man who used to approach the people in kiosks and ask them, and then he died and left behind two dinars.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الصَّفَّةِ: The People of the Kiosk (a group of poor companions who lived in the Prophet's mosque)
key_terms.تَرَكَ كَثِيرًا: He left a lot (referring to the value or significance of his estate/giving)
key_terms.دِينَارَيْنِ: Two dinars (a unit of gold currency)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad say a man who left only two dinars 'left a lot'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the Prophet’s declaration of 'he left a lot' refers not to the material value of the two dinars, but to the spiritual merit of the companion’s consistent habit of giving and seeking to provide for others, specifically the people of the Suffah. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence in conduct) and the intention behind actions, where frequent generosity, even in small amounts, accumulates significant reward. The hadith serves as a reminder that wealth is measured by its utility in fostering community welfare rather than mere accumulation.
